calls.reason: PhysGame reports substantial errors in recognizing physics violations in gameplay videos. That narrow evaluation and the absence of matched GPT-3 retests leave the broader claim insufficiently established.

Wang and Davis report spatial difficulties in o1-preview, alongside improvements. Their studies do not establish frequent elementary errors in released o1 or the asserted explanation for those errors.

The attribution is explicitly hedged. Ars documents human assistance at We Robot, while Ibarz confirms a teleoperated November demonstration and reports autonomous October tasks; the overall share of practical judgment remains unclear.

MIT's RialTo report and RoboCasa show both simulation limitations and benefits in household tasks. Neither establishes that simulation alone cannot supply the required reasoning or that this explains the absence of general-purpose household robots.
